128.literal: A guy who reeks of booze in the middle of the day,
128.official: people don't go putting their faith in guys who reek of alcohol in the middle of the day.

129.literal: I was sure you'd go ahead and order first.
129.official: I was afraid you'd try to order before the client got here.

130.literal: If you'd pulled some breach of etiquette,
130.official: If you got a coffee to sip while you kick back and wait for him to arrive, I'd have slapped the rude right out of you.

131.literal: You've been strictly trained when it comes to manners, huh.
131.official: You guys must get protocol drilled into you pretty hard.

132.literal: Idiot. Your business card's upside down.

133.literal: ...because it won't lead to any deals beyond that.
133.official: If they don't walk away with a business card, you're history to them.

135.literal: From what you've told me, the other party is a typical squatter.
135.official: What you've described sounds like a typical squatter.

136.literal: Yamanoi-san, it was last month that you won the bid on that building?
136.official: You purchased the property at auction last month, correct?

137.literal: So the squatter started settling in just before that?
137.official: Meaning the squatter took up residence just before that?

138.literal: He's a filthy-looking guy, kind of like a homeless man.
138.official: Filthy fellow, looks like he's homeless.

139.literal: Has he demanded a relocation payment from you?
139.official: And has he asked you for a relocation payment yet?

141.literal: If it were me, I wouldn't feel like paying a single penny.
141.official: If it were me, I wouldn't cough up a damn yen.

142.literal: ...or so he says. If things turn into a dispute, I'm scared of what comes after.
142.official: If I put up a fuss now, it could mean worse trouble later.

143.literal: I understand how you feel. But please, rest assured.
143.official: I understand your concern, sir. But please, rest assured.

145.literal: He's a yakuza otaku who's really into it, you see.
145.official: He's a yakuza otaku who really gets into character when he starts nerding out.

146.literal: He gets a real kick out of it. Right, Kiryu-kun?
146.official: Sometimes he likes to play dress-up and pretend he's a real yakuza for the hell of it. Isn't that right, Kiryu-kun?

147.literal: Of course, I'll prepare a separate reward for you all.
147.official: Needless to say, I've also set aside funds to thank you for your services.

151.literal: If you're in real estate, do your homework. Even if a mortgage...
151.official: If you're in real estate, do your homework.

152.literal: ...if you'll do that, we'll cover your moving costs.
152.official: If you agree to move out, we would be happy to cover your expenses.

153.literal: Trying to solve everything with money isn't something I admire.
153.official: And I don't take kindly to you thinking you can throw money at me to make me go away.

154.literal: You trying to pin false accusations on me?
154.official: Are you slinging baseless accusations at me now?

155.literal: Say, Tsuji-san. Why don't we drop this charade?
155.official: C'mon, Tsuji-san. Let's drop the act.

156.literal: Like I said, we don't need that monkey show of yours.
156.official: I told you not to bother with your piss-poor performance.

158.literal: ...Don't get too cocky, you lowly real estate guy.
158.official: You talk an awful big game for a fucking real estate agent.

159.literal: Well then, I've delivered our message, Tsuji-san.
159.official: You have your message. We're done here, Tsuji-san.

160.literal: I thought I'd teach you the ABCs of running the business.
160.official: Right, no time like the present. Let's get you up to speed on the basics of our business.

161.literal: Please go kill some time outside for a bit.
161.official: So, can I ask you to step out for a bit while I get the office put together?

163.literal: Could it be those guys, the Leisure King or whatever he's called?
163.official: They're not related to someone called the Leisure King, are they?

164.literal: ...He was saying dangerous stuff, about getting rid of Yamanoi and beating him up,
164.official: He was talking about driving you out, beating you down... Rough stuff.

165.literal: He's said to be one of the "Five Billionaires."
165.official: Now he's one of the Five Billionaires.

166.literal: Besides the "Leisure King," there's the "Pleasure King," the "Electronics King," the "Gambling King,"
166.official: There's the Leisure King, the Pleasure King, the Electronics King, the Gambling King,

168.literal: have started getting their hands on one Kamurocho property after another.
168.official: They've been snatching up every property in Kamurocho they can.

169.literal: Through pressure and violence, using bad people...
169.official: they use violence and extortion through the thugs they've bought.

170.literal: The five of them divided Kamurocho into five areas,
170.official: The lot of them have sliced Kamurocho up into five areas, each dominion claimed by its respective king.

171.literal: But among those pieces are people working hard, and
171.official: What about the hardworking people on the board trying to live their lives in peace?

172.literal: ...think about it, and the people who live there, and
172.official: The lives of their tenants and the state of Kamurocho don't factor in at all.

173.literal: There are already a great many people who've suffered terribly.
173.official: Their games have already ruined the lives of so many.

174.literal: I want to stop it somehow.
174.official: I want to stop them, if such a thing is even possible.

175.literal: ...With this abnormal boom, it looks like Japan has become prosperous,
175.official: At first glance, you'd think this economy has made Japan a more prosperous place.

176.literal: It could end up becoming a wasteland.
176.official: it'll end up a wasteland, stripped completely bare.

177.literal: I'm a man who has lived a long time alongside this city, too.
177.official: I've shared the better part of my life with this city.

179.literal: That's why I've been resisting them, but...
179.official: That's why I've been fighting them for so long, but...

180.literal: It seems this was too heavy a burden for this old body after all.
180.official: I'm afraid this old body just can't take any more.

182.literal: For the money games of guys like that, Kamurocho...
182.official: The city of Kamurocho deserves better than to get torn apart by a pack of hyenas like them.

183.literal: Of course, I also want to take Kamurocho back from them, and
183.official: Believe me, I'm right there with you in wanting to take the city back from them and restore Kamurocho to the way it was.

184.literal: But the Five Billionaires have an enormous amount of money,
184.official: But the Five Billionaires have more money than you or I can imagine,

185.literal: and they can resort to violence.
185.official: and no compunction about using violence to get what they want.

186.literal: You have the physical strength to stand up to them,
186.official: You have the physical strength to match their goons,

187.literal: a sense of justice that won't let bad people get away with it,
187.official: and a strong sense of uncompromising justice.

188.literal: and the ability to settle disputes.
188.official: You also have the personal skills to minimize loss and resolve conflict.

189.literal: The squatter matter too, which was more than I could handle,
189.official: Take the matter with that squatter. You solved a problem I couldn't handle, in no time flat.

190.literal: If someone like you would take over this office...
190.official: If you were to take over this office... it's possible we might just be able to take a stand against them.

191.literal: What are you talking about... You're overestimating me.
191.official: That's crazy talk. You're giving me way too much credit.
